title: Keyboard Manager: Remapping a shortcut using "right Ctrl"/⇨ with CAN/CSA Z243.200 fails (detected as "VK 223")
author: Chealer
summary: Keyboard Manager treats the Canadian Multilingual Standard bottom-right modifier as ordinary VK 223, preventing it from participating in shortcut remaps as the right-Control-like key users expect.
next_action: Approve a layout-aware modifier classification design and reproduce it with the CMS layout.

confidence.rationale: The failing key identity is known, but the correct Windows scan-code/layout contract must be confirmed on a CMS keyboard or equivalent test layout.

judgment.rationale: The Canadian Multilingual Standard layout reports its bottom-right modifier as VK 223 rather than VK_RCONTROL, and Keyboard Manager consequently records it as an ordinary key instead of a modifier. The issue supplies deterministic steps and a known layout.
evidence: The problem reproduces from PowerToys 0.84.1 through 0.100.2.
Windows/Keyboard Manager exposes the physical bottom-right CMS modifier as VK 223.
The layout documentation and physical placement indicate modifier semantics despite the unusual virtual-key value.
A user demonstrates a workaround by explicitly mapping to VK 223.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a layout-aware modifier classification design and reproduce it with the CMS layout.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Recognize layout-specific modifier keys by physical identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager's shortcut editor classifies modifiers from a fixed virtual-key list, so the CMS layout's VK 223 bottom-right modifier is recorded as a normal key.
plan: Capture scan code, extended-key flag, virtual key, and active keyboard layout when recording shortcut triggers.
Add layout-aware modifier classification for the CMS bottom-right key without changing VK 223 globally.
Persist and replay the physical identity consistently across editor display and runtime matching.
verification: On the Canadian Multilingual Standard layout, record VK 223 plus another key and verify the shortcut triggers.
Switch layouts and verify ordinary VK 223/OEM keys are not incorrectly treated as modifiers.

confidence.rationale: The failing key identity is known, but the correct Windows scan-code/layout contract must be confirmed on a CMS keyboard or equivalent test layout.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager treats the Canadian Multilingual Standard bottom-right modifier as ordinary VK 223, preventing it from participating in shortcut remaps as the right-Control-like key users expect.
known_information: The exact Windows layout is Canadian Multilingual Standard.
The affected physical key is the bottom-right key normally occupied by Right Ctrl.
The report includes deterministic editor and runtime steps.
inferences: Modifier classification is based too narrowly on standard VK_CONTROL variants and ignores layout-specific modifier scan codes.
A scan-code/layout-aware classification can improve editing without globally redefining VK 223.
issue_context.analysis: This is sufficiently scoped for a lightweight design: preserve the recorded physical identity, but classify the key as a modifier only when the active layout reports that role.
